title: Restore substantial scalp hair in severe alopecia areata with systemic treatment

concept.text: Reverse extensive autoimmune hair loss through an approved systemic medicine. JAK-pathway treatment achieved clinically substantial regrowth in a subset of patients, without establishing permanent immune tolerance. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized trials in patients with at least 50% scalp hair loss, demonstrating superiority to placebo in achieving SALT ≤20, equivalent to at least 80% scalp hair coverage. Test set by: FDA; the baricitinib trials evaluated the SALT ≤20 endpoint at week 36. Reported achieved: FDA approved baricitinib (Olumiant) for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. Overlaps: DER-03, IMM-04. Sources given: [FDA announcement of first systemic alopecia areata treatment](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/31bfc85) ; [FDA review describing the alopecia treatment landscape](https://www.fda.gov/media/172964/download?attachment=).
source_urls: [FDA announcement of first systemic alopecia areata treatment](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/31bfc85)

page.title: First approved systemic treatment for severe alopecia areata
page.definition: A medicine that acts throughout the body is approved for adults with severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune attack on hair follicles, after placebo-controlled trials in adults with at least 50% scalp hair loss show that more of them regain at least 80% scalp hair coverage. Hair loss is scored with the Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT), the percentage of the scalp without hair. Benefit is shown during treatment.

goal.need: In 2022, FDA reported that alopecia areata affected more than 300,000 people in the United States each year. In two pivotal trials enrolling adults with at least 50% scalp hair loss for more than six months, only 3–5% of placebo recipients reached at least 80% scalp hair coverage after 36 weeks.

completion.title: FDA approves a systemic medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata on the SALT ≤20 endpoint.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a medicine that acts throughout the body, given by mouth or by injection, with a labelled indication for adults with severe alopecia areata. The approval rests on at least two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in adults with at least 50% scalp hair loss (SALT ≥50) lasting more than 6 months. In each trial a higher proportion of patients on the medicine than on placebo reaches SALT ≤20, at least 80% scalp hair coverage, at week 36. The first such approval meets the test. Topical and intralesional treatments and use outside an approved indication do not count.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: announcement of 13 June 2022, approval letter for NDA 207924/S-007 and prescribing information for Olumiant (baricitinib), sections 1.3 and 14.3, which state the indication, trial population and endpoint.
completion.threshold_quote: Today’s action marks the first FDA approval of a systemic treatment (i.e. treats the entire body rather than a specific location) for alopecia areata.
completion.basis: FDA named this event the first approval of a systemic treatment for alopecia areata, so the test is that first and not an Atlas threshold. The population and endpoint are those of the label's two trials. The test requires superiority to placebo, not a response in most patients: the label reports the proportions reaching SALT ≤20 in each trial. It does not require hair kept after treatment stops, tolerance of the immune system to the follicle, or approval for adolescents.

milestones.title: JAK inhibition restores complete hair coverage in treated mouse skin within 12 weeks.
milestones.criterion: A Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor reverses established alopecia areata in C3H/HeJ mice: treated skin regains complete hair coverage within 12 weeks of the start of treatment and vehicle-treated controls do not, in a peer-reviewed report that states the number of animals per group. This is an animal proof of mechanism. Prevention of disease onset without reversal of established disease is partial.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of FDA approval documents and alopecia areata guidelines found no standardized animal efficacy threshold. The criterion follows the complete-regrowth result in Xing and colleagues' published experiment.

milestones.title: Oral JAK inhibition reduces scalp hair loss by at least 50% in people with alopecia areata.
milestones.criterion: A registered clinical study of an oral JAK inhibitor in patients with moderate-to-severe alopecia areata has as its prespecified primary endpoint the proportion of participants with 50% or greater hair regrowth from baseline, measured by SALT, at the end of treatment, and reports the number of participants who reached it. Regrowth in case reports outside a registered study is partial. An uncontrolled design meets this milestone; it does not establish superiority to placebo.
milestones.set_by: Columbia University investigators, registered protocol NCT01950780, with the prespecified endpoint reported by Mackay-Wiggan and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of subjects with 50% or greater hair regrowth from baseline to end of treatment.

milestones.title: A phase 2 systemic treatment beats placebo for at least 80% scalp coverage at week 36.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in adults with baseline SALT ≥50 shows that a systemic medicine is superior to placebo (P < 0.05) on the proportion of patients reaching SALT ≤20 at week 36, with missing outcomes counted as non-response or handled by another prespecified method.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company and BRAVE-AA1 investigators, phase 2 protocol NCT03570749, reported by King and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving a Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score ≤20 at week 36.

milestones.title: Systemic treatment beats placebo for ≥80% scalp coverage at week 36 in two phase 3 trials.
milestones.criterion: Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in adults with baseline SALT ≥50 each show that a systemic medicine is superior to placebo on the primary endpoint, the proportion of patients reaching SALT ≤20 at week 36, and the results are published after peer review or reported in regulator-approved labelling. One trial is partial.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company and BRAVE-AA investigators, phase 3 protocols NCT03570749 and NCT03899259; FDA reports the regulatory response estimates in prescribing-information section 14.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary outcome was a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36.

not_found: No regulator or professional-society threshold for preclinical hair-regrowth efficacy was found.
The supplied FDA review at media/172964 could not be opened because its PDF exceeded the retrieval size limit.
No public FDA authorization letter for the initial alopecia areata clinical trials was found.

results.finding: C3H/HeJ mice with established alopecia areata: 9 per treatment group; complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks.
results.detail: Topical ruxolitinib and tofacitinib were applied to affected back skin. Each treatment and vehicle group included three mice per experiment across three experiments.
results.quote: A full coat of hair emerged in the ruxolitinib- or tofacitinib-treated mice by 7 weeks of treatment (data not shown), and we observed complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks following topical therapy (

results.finding: Oral ruxolitinib: 9 of 12 patients (75%) achieved at least 50% hair regrowth by SALT at the end of treatment.
results.detail: Registered study NCT01950780 prespecified the SALT-based responder proportion as its primary endpoint. Treatment lasted 3–6 months. The open-label, uncontrolled design does not establish superiority to placebo.
results.quote: Nine of twelve patients (75%) had significant hair regrowth and achieved the primary outcome of at least 50% regrowth

results.finding: Baricitinib phase 2 trial (N=110): at week 36, SALT ≤20 was achieved by 51.9% on 4 mg versus 3.6% on placebo (P=.001).
results.detail: Adults had baseline scalp hair loss ≥50%; treatment was randomized and placebo-controlled, with nonresponder imputation for missing data. The supplied text does not establish double blinding.
results.quote: At week 36, the proportion of patients achieving a SALT score of ≤20 was significantly greater in baricitinib 2-mg (33.3%, P = .016) and 4-mg (51.9%, P = .001) groups versus placebo (3.6%).

results.finding: Oral baricitinib 4 mg increased week-36 SALT ≤20 response over placebo by 32.6 percentage points in both BRAVE-AA1 (n=654) and BRAVE-AA2 (n=546).
results.detail: Both randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolled adults with baseline SALT ≥50 and met the primary endpoint (P<0.001 for each dose versus placebo). The supplied text does not establish that the trials were double-blind.
results.quote: The estimated percentage of patients with a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36 was 38.8% with 4-mg baricitinib, 22.8% with 2-mg baricitinib, and 6.2% with placebo in BRAVE-AA1 and 35.9%, 19.4%, and 3.3%, respectively, in BRAVE-AA2.

results.finding: Topical ruxolitinib or tofacitinib restored complete hair coverage within 12 weeks in C3H/HeJ mice with established alopecia areata (3 mice per group).
results.detail: The report describes vehicle controls and three repetitions, but the supplied text does not explicitly state that vehicle-treated skin failed to regain complete coverage.
results.quote: A full coat of hair emerged in the ruxolitinib- or tofacitinib-treated mice by 7 weeks of treatment (data not shown), and we observed complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks following topical therapy

results.finding: Oral ruxolitinib produced near-complete hair regrowth in all 3 patients with moderate-to-severe alopecia areata within 3–5 months.
results.detail: These were the first three participants in registered open-label study NCT01950780. The text does not establish a prespecified SALT ≥50% improvement primary endpoint or report its responder count at the end of treatment.
results.quote: All three ruxolitinib-treated patients exhibited near-complete hair regrowth within 3 to 5 months of oral treatment

results.finding: Oral ruxolitinib: 9 of 12 patients (75%) achieved at least 50% scalp hair regrowth by SALT at the end of treatment.
results.detail: Registered study NCT01950780 prespecified the SALT responder endpoint. Treatment lasted 3–6 months. The open-label, uncontrolled design meets m2 but does not establish superiority to placebo.
results.quote: Nine of twelve patients (75%) had significant hair regrowth and achieved the primary outcome of at least 50% regrowth

results.finding: Oral baricitinib 4 mg in BRAVE-AA1 phase 2 (110 adults randomized) increased week-36 SALT ≤20 response by 48.3 percentage points versus placebo.
results.detail: Randomized, double-blind trial in adults with baseline SALT ≥50. Responses were 14/27 versus 1/28 (P=0.001), using nonresponder imputation. AA-IGA 0/1 corresponds to SALT ≤20. This is a sponsor's regulatory submission, not a peer-reviewed paper or regulator's finding.

results.finding: FDA approved oral baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata (two trials, n=1,200); 35% on 4 mg achieved the coverage endpoint in AA-1.
results.detail: First systemic FDA approval, June 13, 2022. Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials enrolled patients with ≥50% scalp hair loss. At week 36, ≥80% coverage (SALT ≤20) occurred with 4 mg in 35% versus 5% on placebo in AA-1 and 32% versus 3% in AA-2.
results.quote: Today’s action marks the first FDA approval of a systemic treatment (i.e. treats the entire body rather than a specific location) for alopecia areata.
